item.title: Someone Has to Be New at This
item.description: AI can help new engineers finish today’s change, but output alone does not build the understanding and judgment needed to own tomorrow’s problem. Teams should preserve consequential work, explanation, independent diagnosis, feedback, revision, and progressively greater responsibility.

item.title: The Model Release Experiment: From Intuition to Inspectable Evidence
item.description: What GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna add to a frozen-task experiment, how to inspect each saved profile, and why one response per profile establishes neither a universal ranking nor a causal setting effect.

item.title: The Model Release Experiment
item.description: Why The Model Release Experiment keeps one frozen story-and-math task, where readers can inspect model cards and run pages, and why receipt checks cover arithmetic rather than overall response quality.

item.title: What Prompt Precision Bought in 24 Agent Trials
item.description: Observed: All 24 trials in this small synthetic study met the full intended specification on the first pass. Spelling-error mean output stayed within 2% of clear; reduced-grammar runs used 5% more output for Task A and 18% more for Task B; ambiguous-rule runs used 9% more and 27% more. Interpretation: Ambiguous rules transferred rule selection to the agent, so specify governing rules, exceptions, invariants, and success checks first. The one-model, two-task sample, conventional intended answers, non-causal design, and all-success ceiling do not show that ambiguity is safe or that surface form never matters.

item.title: What I Mean by AI Alignment and Why I Expect It to Improve
item.description: Why I expect AI alignment to improve, what benchmark results can establish, and whether refusing unsafe instructions belongs in the definition.

item.title: The Two-Model Pruning Cycle: How to Simplify an AI-Assisted Codebase Safely
item.description: A practical two-reviewer cycle for pruning an AI-assisted codebase: reconcile independent evidence, make one reversible change, and audit the behavior it must preserve.

item.title: What Chip Restrictions May Be Teaching China
item.description: Restricted and uncertain compute access can reduce experiments while making efficiency more valuable. Chinese model disclosures show adaptation, but not that chip controls caused innovation or improved the odds of breakthroughs, including any path to AGI.

item.title: The Limit May Not Be in the Model
item.description: An inherited product default can constrain how model capability reaches users. Review it as a versioned product contract with an accountable owner, task-specific evaluation, decision evidence, a canary against a control, and a trigger for reconsideration.

item.title: Context + Prompt = Anything a Computer Can Do
item.description: A prompt can name a change but cannot complete it alone; context, tools, permission, feedback, and claim-matched verification turn an instruction into trustworthy computer work.

item.title: Apple Is Not Positioned for Future Endeavors
item.description: Apple's September Siri AI beta is meaningful progress, but its documented access limits leave a dated concern: Apple's integrated operating model may still slow AI delivery until broad, reliable product results prove otherwise.

item.title: I Built an AI Telemetry System Because My Memory Is Too Forgiving
item.description: Why I built a longitudinal record to challenge my forgiving memory, guide decisions about standards, rework, subscription economics, and project attention, without treating activity as achievement.

item.title: The Machine Did Exactly What You Asked
item.description: A seeded optimizer gamed its score, one live agent repaired an apparent intent gap, and another obeyed a false criterion. These small historical demonstrations lead to a practical contract test for concrete AI goals.

item.title: From Idea to Verified URL: Build a Blog Workflow That Still Sounds Like You
item.description: Build an inspectable AI-assisted article workflow with observable artifacts, evidence-based voice controls, scoped publication, live verification, and a clear boundary between verified publication and search indexing.
